assessment: The study uses an elegant CRISPR/Cas9 screening approach in a myeloid cell line to identify the underlying regulators of the alarmins S100A8 and S100A9, which amplify inflammation. This approach identified the transcription factor C/EBP-δ as a regulator of S100A8 and S100A9 expression in the myeloid cell line and also showed a correlation between the expression levels of C/EBP-δ and the alarmins in patient samples of peripheral blood mononuclear cells. Furthermore, the authors also validate their findings in primary monocytes using mice with genetic C/EBP-δ deletion. This work will be of significant interest to researchers studying the regulation of immune responses and inflammation, and it also highlights how unbiased CRISPR/Cas9 screening can lead to novel mechanistic insights in myeloid cells.
